transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Um, well, I guess it really started getting overwhelming recently. I'm an artist, mostly mixed media and collage work, and my family asked me to put together a memorial piece for my aunt who passed away. She was just this incredibly vibrant, wonderful person, really a huge presence in my life, so obviously I wanted the piece to be absolutely perfect for the service. 

But... it wasn't just my usual artistic perfectionism, which is why I finally decided to come in. While I was working on it, I just kept getting these awful, completely unwanted thoughts. They would just invade my head. I kept thinking that I was going to dishonor her somehow. I'd be sitting there at my drafting table, and my brain would just insist that one wrong photo placement, or, you know, choosing the wrong color for the matting, would mean I didn't actually love her enough. Like if I put a picture of her from the nineties next to one from her wedding, it would be this massive disrespect to her entire legacy. 

And, I mean, as an artist, I'm totally used to second-guessing myself. I have creative doubts all the time about composition or lighting. But I couldn't just brush these thoughts off like normal creative doubts. They felt so heavy and loud, and I'd just sit there agonizing over a single piece of paper for hours because the thought of ruining her memory was just looping in my head. I just couldn't snap out of it and it really scared me, to be honest.

When you had those upsetting thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, did you feel driven to do something over and over again—like checking, arranging, or redoing parts of the memorial—to try to make the anxiety go away or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, exactly. It is exactly like that, and honestly it is incredibly frustrating because I know, logically, that the piece is fine. I have been doing this for years, I know how to compose a piece, you know? But when that heavy, awful feeling hits, when that thought about dishonoring her just spikes in my chest... I just can not leave it alone. 

I will be sitting there at my drafting table, and I will have these little typed-out labels for the different eras of her life, and I will end up rereading the label text over and over and over again. Just staring at it, reading the exact same few words, trying to make sure there is not some hidden mistake that is going to ruin the whole tribute. And then with the photos and the matting, I will start nudging the same objects on the table. Like, just moving a photo a tiny fraction of an inch to the left, and then back to the right, and then back again, just tapping it with my finger. 

I always take these layout photos on my phone to check the overall composition, which is a totally normal artist thing to do, but then I am checking the layout photos over and over, zooming in, zooming out, comparing the screen to the physical board. I just keep doing it, all of it, the reading, the nudging, the checking, until it finally just feels settled in my brain. It has to feel right, or the anxiety just keeps building. And the absolute worst part is that part of me is sitting there watching myself do this, totally aware that it is already fine, that the layout is perfectly balanced, and I am just losing studio time. I mean, natural daylight is so important for color matching, and I will just waste an entire afternoon nudging a single piece of cardstock. It is just so exhausting to lose that much time to something when I know the art is actually finished, but I just can not move on to the next step until my brain gives me the okay.
